title: Notification System
summary: A notification system turns product events ("your order shipped", "Sam replied") into push, email, and SMS messages without spamming people. It checks each user's preferences and quiet hours, queues work by channel and priority, delivers through third-party providers with retries, and uses delivery and bounce feedback to clean up bad addresses and tokens.

walkthrough.title: Product emits an event
walkthrough.text: A service calls the notification API: notify user 42 with template order_shipped and some data. An idempotency key makes retries safe.

walkthrough.title: Check preferences
walkthrough.text: The API loads the user's opt-ins per category and channel, quiet hours, time zone, and device tokens. Marketing to an opted-out user stops here; a security alert is always sent.

walkthrough.title: Enqueue per channel
walkthrough.text: Each delivery is rendered from its template and placed on a channel queue (push, email, SMS) with a priority. A password reset never waits behind a newsletter.

walkthrough.title: Workers pick up jobs
walkthrough.text: Channel workers pull jobs at the rate each provider allows, batch low-priority messages into digests, and deduplicate repeats.

walkthrough.title: Send via providers
walkthrough.text: Workers call APNs or FCM for push, SES or SendGrid for email, Twilio for SMS. Transient failures retry with backoff; permanent ones go to a dead-letter queue.

walkthrough.title: Collect delivery feedback
walkthrough.text: Providers report delivered, bounced, unsubscribed, or invalid token through webhooks. Opens and clicks are tracked too.

walkthrough.title: Clean up targets
walkthrough.text: Hard-bounced emails, dead device tokens, and spam complaints update the preference store, so the next send skips them and sender reputation stays healthy.

data.label: Product Services
responsibilities: Decides that something happened worth telling a user about.
Sends intent (template + data), not finished emails or push payloads.
Tags each notification with a category such as transactional, social, or marketing.

failureModes.scenario: Event replayed after a bug fix
failureModes.impact: Users get the same notification twice, or ten times.
failureModes.mitigation: Idempotency key per logical notification, deduplicated at the API.

failureModes.scenario: Bulk job emits a million events at once
failureModes.impact: Queues flood and urgent messages are delayed.
failureModes.mitigation: Separate bulk lanes and per-producer quotas.

data.label: Notification API
responsibilities: Validates, deduplicates, and decides which channels each notification goes to.
Renders localised templates per channel (push title, email HTML, 160-character SMS).
Applies quiet hours and per-user frequency caps by scheduling sends for later.

failureModes.impact: Every notification is delayed behind the lookup.
failureModes.mitigation: Cache preferences; if lookup fails, send transactional messages and defer marketing ones.
Template tests with sample data, staged rollout, and sending to internal users first.

data.label: Preferences & Targets
responsibilities: Stores what each user wants per category and channel: the source of truth for consent.
Keeps device tokens, verified emails, and phone numbers.
Records unsubscribes immediately, as laws like CAN-SPAM and GDPR require.

failureModes.impact: Legal exposure, spam complaints, damaged sender reputation.
failureModes.mitigation: Synchronous write on unsubscribe, checked at send time and not only at enqueue time.

failureModes.impact: Wasted sends, and providers may throttle you.
failureModes.mitigation: Remove tokens that providers report as invalid.

data.label: Channel Queues

input.name: Jobs
input.type: One per (user, channel), keyed by userId

responsibilities: Buffers bursts so providers receive a steady rate.
Separates urgent (OTP, security) from bulk (digest, marketing) traffic.
Holds delayed jobs for quiet hours and scheduled sends.

failureModes.impact: OTP codes arrive after they expire.
failureModes.mitigation: Dedicated high-priority queues and workers that bulk traffic cannot use.
Retry limit, then dead-letter queue with alerting.

data.label: Delivery Workers

output.name: Provider calls
output.type: APNs HTTP/2, FCM v1, SES SendEmail, Twilio Messages

responsibilities: Sends at each provider's allowed rate and retries transient errors with backoff.
Collapses multiple notifications into digests ("5 new comments").
Fails over to a backup provider when the primary degrades.

failureModes.scenario: Retry after a timeout that actually succeeded
failureModes.impact: Duplicate SMS, which also costs money.
failureModes.mitigation: Pass idempotency keys to providers that support them; record each send before retrying.

failureModes.impact: Sends fail and queues back up.
failureModes.mitigation: Adaptive rate limiting driven by provider responses; secondary provider for SMS and email.

data.label: Channel Providers

input.name: Send
input.type: Push payload, MIME email, SMS body

responsibilities: Deliver to the device, the inbox, or the carrier network.
Enforce their own rate limits, content rules, and sender reputation.
Report delivery results asynchronously.

failureModes.scenario: Email domain lands in spam folders
failureModes.mitigation: SPF/DKIM/DMARC, a separate sending domain for marketing, and fast bounce suppression.
Registered sender IDs, per-country routing, and fallback to voice or another provider.

data.label: Delivery Tracking

output.name: Updates
output.type: Suppress email, drop token, delivery status

responsibilities: Records each notification's lifecycle: sent, delivered, opened, clicked.
Suppresses hard bounces and spam complaints immediately.
Measures delivery rate per channel and provider for alerting.

failureModes.impact: Bounced addresses keep receiving mail; reputation falls.
failureModes.mitigation: Queue webhooks durably on receipt; reconcile with provider suppression lists.

failureModes.scenario: Open tracking blocked by mail privacy features
failureModes.mitigation: Use clicks and conversions as the main engagement signal.
